formulations.label: Cream (muscle rub)
formulations.strengths: Menthol 2.54%, camphor 1.41%, methyl salicylate 0.42% w/w (plus white camphor oil 0.32% and capsicum oleoresin 0.005% w/w)
formulations.note: UK SmPC for a muscle rub cream that contains all three clinic ingredients plus a fourth active, capsicum oleoresin; its methyl salicylate content is only 0.42%. The clinic products' strengths are not given in the clinic list, so check the label: a higher methyl salicylate content may raise the salicylate absorption and toxicity risk. Contains cetostearyl alcohol, lanolin and sodium laurilsulfate (local skin reactions).

src.q: Menthol 2.54% w/w Camphor 1.41% w/w Methyl Salicylate 0.42% w/w
Oleoresin Capsicum 500,000 Water soluble (equivalent to 0.000125% capsaicin) 0.005% w/w
The excipients cetostearyl alcohol, lanolin and 0.91% w/w sodium laurilsulfate may cause local skin reactions
Camphor Oil, White 0.32%w/w

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Symptomatic relief of muscular and rheumatic aches and pains, including muscular stiffness, bruising, sprains and fibrositis.

src.q: For the symptomatic relief of muscular and rheumatic aches and pains, including; muscular stiffness, bruising, sprains, fibrositis.

restrictions.note: The UK SmPC for the muscle rub cream states no prescribing restriction beyond the age limit.

items.t: Apply to the affected area and massage slowly into the skin. For muscular strains and stiffness it works best after a hot bath. No frequency or maximum is stated.
items.tag: Adults, elderly and children over 6 years

src.q: Apply to the affected parts and slowly massage well into the skin.
For muscular strains and stiffness it is best used after a hot bath.
Elderly The adult dose is appropriate.

items.t: Contraindicated in children under 6 years. Children over 6 years: adult dose.

src.q: Not to be used on children under 6 years old.
Adults and children over 6 Apply to the affected parts

items.t: Children are at higher risk of serious poisoning: under 10 years have a higher risk of salicylate toxicity, and camphor deaths in children have been recorded from 1 g. Keep out of the sight and reach of children.

src.q: Patients under ten years or over 70 have increased risk of salicylate toxicity
fatalities in children have been recorded from 1g
Keep out of the sight and reach of children.

items.t: Children under 6 years; skin abrasions or irritated skin; hypersensitivity to salicylates or any other ingredient. Stop if irritation develops.

src.q: Not to be used on children under 6 years old. Do not apply to skin abrasions. Do not apply to irritated skin.
Contraindicated in patients who are hypersensitive to salicylates or to any other ingredient in the preparation.
If irritation develops, use of the product should be discontinued.

items.t: Systemic salicylate poisoning has been reported after application to large areas of skin or for long periods. Patients under 10 or over 70 years are at higher risk of salicylate toxicity.

src.q: symptoms of systemic salicylate poisoning have been reported after the application of salicylates to large areas of skin or for prolonged periods
Patients under ten years or over 70 have increased risk of salicylate toxicity

items.t: Keep away from the eyes and sensitive areas. For external use only. If symptoms persist, see a doctor.

src.q: Keep away from eyes and sensitive areas. If symptoms persist consult a doctor.
For external use only.

items.t: Fire hazard: fabric (clothing, bedding, dressings) that has been in contact with the cream burns more easily; patients must not smoke or go near naked flames. Washing reduces but does not remove build-up.

src.q: Instruct patients not to smoke or go near naked flames - risk of severe burns.
Fabric (clothing, bedding, dressings etc) that has been in contact with this product burns more easily and is a serious fire hazard.

items.t: Warfarin: there are reports that topical salicylates may increase the anticoagulant effect of warfarin. Menthol taken by mouth has been reported to reduce the effect of warfarin. No action is stated.

src.q: There have been reports that topical salicylates may potentiate the anticoagulant effects of warfarin.
Menthol has also been reported to interact with warfarin (when taken orally), decreasing its effectiveness.

renal.note: The UK SmPC for the muscle rub cream gives no renal advice for the cream (renal failure is listed only as a feature of salicylate poisoning).

hepatic.note: The UK SmPC for the muscle rub cream gives no hepatic advice.

items.t: No or inadequate evidence of safety in pregnancy; as a precaution, use only when there is no safer alternative.

src.q: There is no, or inadequate evidence of safety in human pregnancy or lactation.
should only be used during pregnancy or lactation when there is no safer alternative

items.t: No or inadequate evidence of safety in breastfeeding; as a precaution, use only when there is no safer alternative.

src.q: There is no, or inadequate evidence of safety in human pregnancy or lactation.

reproductive.note: The UK SmPC for the muscle rub cream gives no fertility or contraception advice.

items.t: No frequencies given. Menthol: contact dermatitis or eczema, hypersensitivity with urticaria, flushing and headache. Capsicum oleoresin can irritate the skin.

src.q: Known side effects of menthol - contact dermatitis or eczema, hypersensitivity reactions characterised by urticaria, flushing and headache.
Irritation of the skin may also be caused by the capsicum oleoresin in this product.

items.t: Any adverse reaction: stop use immediately.

src.q: If an adverse reaction occurs discontinue use immediately.

items.t: Salicylate poisoning (large areas, prolonged use or ingestion): vomiting, dehydration, tinnitus, vertigo, deafness, sweating, fast breathing; acid-base disturbance. Measure plasma salicylate.

src.q: Common features include vomiting, dehydration, tinnitus, vertigo, deafness, sweating, warm extremities with bounding pulses, increased respiratory rate and hyperventilation.
The plasma salicylate concentration should be measured

items.t: Camphor or menthol poisoning (ingestion or excessive use): nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, delirium, twitching, convulsions, CNS depression and coma; deaths in children from 1 g of camphor.

src.q: Ingestion of the product or excessive use may also lead to camphor poisoning
delirium, muscle twitching, epileptiform convulsions, CNS depression and coma
fatalities in children have been recorded from 1g

items.t: Stop if skin irritation or any adverse reaction develops; see a doctor if symptoms persist.

src.q: If irritation develops, use of the product should be discontinued.
If symptoms persist consult a doctor.

items.t: External use only. Massage slowly into the affected area. Use sparingly on tender skin and do not cover straight after applying. Wash hands thoroughly after use.

src.q: Use sparingly on tender skin and do not cover immediately after application.
Wash hands thoroughly after use.

items.t: Do not use on broken or irritated skin, near the eyes, or on large areas for long periods. Keep the tube away from children (camphor and salicylate are dangerous if swallowed). Do not smoke or go near flames: fabric with cream on it catches fire easily.

src.q: Do not apply to skin abrasions. Do not apply to irritated skin.
Keep out of the sight and reach of children.
Instruct patients not to smoke or go near naked flames - risk of severe burns.
